displayName: PPMCP-R1 pinned upstream pancake-pos-mcp and legacy delta re-intake
priorAbsorption: pancake-pos-mcp already had a prior partial disposition trail before this wave: W3 tool-action taxonomy absorbed business tool registry, approval gate, and action-risk concepts (docs/reference/archive/CVF_LEGACY_HARVEST_CLOSEOUT_LEDGER_2026-05-25.md line 141, PARTIALLY_ABSORBED); LHW16-T2 closed a narrow MCP-approval-proof-advisory reopen condition doc-only (docs/reference/archive/CVF_LHW16_T2_MCP_APPROVAL_PROOF_ADVISORY_CONNECTOR_SPEC_2026-05-30.md); a legacy-spec-absorption registry row marked the generic MCP business adapter as runtime-owned absorbed with the Pancake-specific profile deferred (docs/reference/archive/CVF_LEGACY_SPEC_ABSORPTION_REGISTRY_2026-05-23.md line 120). None of these prior dispositions used a pinned upstream source mirror or a full 107-file comparison; PPMCP-R1 supersedes them with a file-level comparison against the current EXTENSIONS/CVF_EXECUTION_PLANE_FOUNDATION/src/mcp.business.adapter.contract.ts and governance/contracts/tool-action-taxonomy.ts owner surfaces.

findings.summary: Legacy mcp-business-transport-policy.ts couples transport choice to risk level; the current mcp.business.adapter.contract.ts evaluateTransport() only checks the allowedTransports allowlist, with no risk-aware transport gating.
findings.nextAction: Reviewer/operator decides whether to open a fresh runtime work order to add risk-aware transport gating.

findings.summary: Upstream per-tool discriminated action schemas perform runtime parsing of action-specific input variants; the current CVF MCP business contract carries opaque inputSchema and outputSchema records without a runtime validation call.
findings.nextAction: Park a provider-neutral action-schema validation candidate; reopen only after a concrete invalid-input or schema-drift problem and fresh runtime authorization.

findings.summary: Upstream compact response projection (json-mask-based, measured 26.8%-63.1% byte reduction in tests/replay/report.md) has no current CVF owner surface for MCP response-size or context-budget shaping.
findings.nextAction: Reviewer decides on conditional reopen index entry for a future value probe.

findings.summary: Upstream orders-tool.ts resolveOrderDisplayId implements a two-stage safe display-ID-to-internal-ID resolver with structured error codes before a destructive mutation; no CVF owner surface addresses safe entity targeting before destructive action.
findings.nextAction: Reviewer decides on conditional reopen index entry pending a concrete CVF-native need.

findings.summary: Upstream tests/replay/ and tests/fixtures/orders-delete/ implement production-trace replay regression and negative-mutation-fixture testing patterns with no CVF equivalent for MCP-adjacent adapter tests.
findings.nextAction: Reviewer decides on conditional reopen index entry as a checker candidate, parked until a concrete repeated defect is demonstrated.

findings.summary: CVF's current stableStringify-based key-sorted receipt hashing and deterministic receiptId are already more rigorous than both the legacy proposal's and the upstream repository's plain JSON.stringify-based hashing; no delta to absorb, CVF surface is ahead.
findings.nextAction: None; recorded for completeness so the comparison is not silently one-directional.

findings.summary: Direct import of all 24 upstream tool implementations, transport entry points, HTTP client, and resource registry is rejected; CVF has no live MCP execution runtime to consume Pancake-specific business logic.
findings.nextAction: None; direct import remains rejected without fresh CVF authorization.
